   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use

welcome direct correspondence

From: D.J. Wood, CAMBRIDGE

I read with great interest your
recent article on Spectrum +2
with Amstrad colour monitor
contributed by Mr. Malcolm
Perry. I use my +2 with a Micro-
vitec 'Cub' but only get eight

I enjoy my OUTLETS very much -
please keep up the good work and
I hope your financial problems
sort themselves out. I've
recommended your disc magazine
to several friends who had not
heard of you.

It may be of interest to anyone
with a 'sick' Spectrum...

 N.R. Baldwell Electronics
 288, Abbeydale Road,
 SHEFFIELD S7 1FL

keep coming back to the Spectrum

world to touch OUTLET. I would

Happy Christmas.

         David J. Wood

Brian Cavers to David Wood

Thanks, David. We have passed on
your letter to Malcolm Perry.

                        - Brian

From: Stephen Baines, SHEFFIELD

Dear OUTLET,

In Issue 63 there was a letter
from G.A. Jones regarding the
FD-9 disc drive. I purchased one
of these from Greenweld Electro-
nics and it is a wonderful drive
made FOR Amstrad by one of the
larger disc drive manufacturers.
It is VERY quiet, and VERY
reliable.

Setting it up involves removing
the case (6 bolts), unplugging
the power lead, and the data
lead. There is a little surface
mount switch marked "0" and "1",
this equates to "1" and "2" on
the +D/Disciple.


You can use it as a second drive
by purchasing a BBC Data lead
from:

Cambridge Computer Science,
374, Milton Road,
Cambridge, CB4 1SU

for `5.29 (ask for a DUAL 3.5"
BBC DATA LEAD).

The power supply is relatively
simple. I run it from the
cassette power socket inside the
Spectrum as this is already
regulated, alternatively, you
can buy a 5v PSU from CCS for
`5.64.

The power lead that comes with
the drive has 4 connections.


You only need to connect two
which are the same as the ones
on the original drive that comes
with the +D.

Slot the cables through the case
and then replace the case.

It is quite larger, 110 x 210 x
35mm, but will stand on the tape
deck of a +2A. It is quicker
than the +D drive, it has a
stepping rate of 6ms. Yes, it is
a 2MB drive, but when you use
DSDD discs, it formats them as
normal. The use of a DSHD disc
would only format half of the
disc, and be unusable on a
"normal" DSDD drive. I've used
mine now for 3 months and have
had no problems.


Regarding "utilizing" and
"utilising", the preface to the
OED 1990 (8th Edition) states:

 "English is a language that has
  an exceptional tolerance of
  variations in spelling
  (generalise and generalize,
  and so on)."

In the 1400-1700 period "s" was
mainly used. In the 1700's the
"z" took hold, in the 1800's it
was swaying back to "s".In 1900,
the OED "z'de" [unreadable -
probably "zedded"! -Ed.] the
lot, and over the past 90 years
it has swung more to the "s", as
the English have a natural
dislike of the "z" [? again, un-
readable -Ed.] an 'ugly' letter.


The "z" isn't an Americanism,
but a curiosity of the English
printers and Dr. Johnson.

       Yours faithfully,

        Stephen Baines

From: D.A. Turton, LIVERPOOL

Dear Ron and Brian,

I enjoyed the Video Title prog-
ram in Issue 63, the only fault
is, I couldn't get the mega-size
print to work, as all it would
do as soon as you tried to type
any kind of message was to just
crash the program, everything
else seems to work o.k.

Now, regarding the increase in
the price of your OUTLET disks,
I have read every letter pub-
lished, as well as your comments
on the subject, and I just don't
see any argument. Where in this
world would anyone get a disk or
tape of the quality that you


publish for the price we pay,
(even if it were `4.50 or `5.00
per Issue?) The people who
'quibble' over paying such a
small increase must be mad to
say the least, let's see them
produce a programmed disk or
tape of the same quality even at
double the price.

Well, Ron and Brian, that's my
feelings, and I must admit I
feel a lot better for getting
that off my chest. May I wish
you and all your colleagues a
MERRY CHRISTMAS AND A HAPPY AND
PROSPEROUS NEW YEAR.

       Yours faithfully,

          D.A. Turton

Brian Cavers to D.A. Turton

Sorry, the mega-text problem in
VIDEO-DIT seems to be a +3 or at
least a 128K mode problem.If you
press BREAK at the title page
and then enter SPECTRUM followed
by GO TO 8905 you will find it
works ok in 48K BASIC. You might
alternatively, MERGE in ROUTE 48
(OUTLET 31) which switches to 48
mode.Sorry I don't have a better
solution but it's usually a huge
job to hack through machine code
like this program is to find out
what is going wrong!

                        - Brian

From: M.D. Atkins, 70 Rudgwick

Dear Ron and Brian,

Regarding Bill Clark's letter in
OUTLET No 64, I have version 2
(01.09.88) of TASPRINT +3 which
runs quite well with version
2.06 (04.04.89) of TASWORD +3.
My only complaint is that
TASPRINT +3 only supports 8/9
pin printers and therefore the
quality of the printout from a
24-pin printer is somewhat
disappointing.

If Bill has the same versions of
these utilities I would be quite
prepared to look at them to see
whether he has set his TASPRINT
program the same as mine.


I've also experienced a similar
printing problem with MASTERFILE
+3 but, in fairness, the printer
options are quite good for 8/9
pin printers.These include sett-
ing the left margin, 6, 8 or 10
lines per inch, a choice of
International character set,
different character sizes,
emphasised printing etc.

It is possible to utilise 24-pin
printers by converting the MF+3
data into ASCII data and then
merging this into TASWORD +3 and
the full range of options for 24
pin printers then becomes
available.

          M.D. Atkins

         Malcolm Perry,
       216, Marlpool Lane,
  Kidderminster, Worcs DY11 5DL

Dear Ron and Brian,

Re: SCPDSA
When I did not receive expected
issues of the above disc I wrote
and had the "standard" reply
that because SAMCo had failed
SCPDSA had ceased trading. The
impression I had was that SCPDSA
was part of SAMCo. However, I
was sure SCPDSA was independent
and not part of SAMCo,therefore,
I wrote and asked for a refund
of the subs I had just paid. It
went through my mind that a firm
could simply decide to finish
and pocket any money sent.

Having no reply to my letter I
contacted the Trading Standards
Office at Kingston upon Thames
and asked them if they knew if
SCPDSA had ceased trading as
part of SAMCo or if they'd "just
decided" to finish. I mentioned
I'd asked for a refund of out-
standing subs but had not had a
reply.The Trading office 'phoned
back and said they had spoken to
SCPDSA and they had agreed to
refund the subs.

Therefore, I suggest if anyone
has anything outstanding (i.e.
not received full number of
issues for subs. paid) that you
ask for outstanding refunds. If
you do not get satisfaction then
let the Trading Standards Office
know at...

GUILD HALL,Kingston upon Thames,
SURREY. KT1 1EU. 081 547 6499.
(For attention of Mrs Coventry).

I know it might seem a bit of
fuss over just a few pounds but
it is the principle that you
cannot take money then simply
decide not to supply the goods.
My refund has been used to try a
bit of advertising for OUTLET in
the local press. Time will only
tell if it did any good but at
least if you do not try you will
never know.

I am afraid this letter is some-
what downbeat and reflects the
negative side of computing.I can
only hope that those responsible


begin to rethink and consider as
such attitudes can only, in the
long term,damage the public view
of the SAM Scene.

It was mentioned in OUTLET rec-
cently that SAM PSUs were avail-
able from GREENWELD for `9.95
(order code Z9111) plus postage
per order of `2.75. However, a
comment in a recent FORMAT tends
to throw some doubt as to the
desirability of these items,
stating it seems that they are
not "official units" and to be
treated with suspicion. Let me
confirm that GREENWELD have been
going now for quite a few years
and are a reputable company,I've
dealt with them over a number of
years and have no complaints.

As an example, when the electric
ignition on our central heating
boiler and gas fire failed the
"official" replacement cost `30
which was a lot of money in the
1970s. I had a couple of spark
igniters from Greenweld for
about `5 and they are still both
working well.

The firm deals mainly in electr-
onic items but also diverges in-
to such as stationery, drawing
office items ond so on.They have
a "main line" catalogue of items
held in stock. They also deal in
manufactures surplus and bank-
rupt stock bought via receivers
and etc. This is, as they said
in their recent news sheet, that
these PSUs came via "official"


route through the receivers when
SAMCO failed.

Such items are obviously trans-
itional so do not form part of
their main catalogue but are
notified in monthly sheets
available on subscription or by
telephoning Newsline (0891 505
121). Remember this is the
36p/48p min rate.

Therefore, I see no reason to be
"suspicious" that they are sell-
ing SAM PSUs at well below the
"standard" price. It is simply
that the firm passes on items at
prices that reflect what they
paid for them and are not out to
make vast profits. (Some profit,
yes, but not over the top).


Obviously, those selling SAM
PSUs at over `20 would not be
too happy at being under-cut and
no doubt try to discourage
prospective purchasers from
saving money.

Would an "official" supplier, if
had had the chance to purchase
the items via the receiver, have
passed them on at a price refl-
ecting what they paid, or at the
"official" price?

The only defence is that
"official" suppliers in the SAM
circle only really cater to a
relatively small group and so
would only sell an odd power
supply now and again. Greenweld
deal in bulk quantities(SAM PSUs


are even cheaper if you buy 100
at a unit price of `4.40 +VAT
and postage) and circulate to a
larger, prospective purchaser
group with general electronic
interests,therefore,able to make
less profit per item which is
compensated for by quantity
sales. As regards "SAMCOs soak
test?" - myself having had a
number of "official" units that
were faulty only speaks for
itself.

If you still have any doubts or
queries as to the serviceability
or guarantee of a particular
item purchased from Greenweld
then ring them on 0703 236363
GREENWELD ELECTRONICS LTD. 27
PARK ROAD. SOUTHAMPTON. SO1 3TB.


While mentioning FORMAT,has any-
one else had problems over the
promise to convert S&SC subs to
those of FORMAT? I have, and
they have declined to answer why
over the last 3 to 4 months.


The Trading Office has said that
Format is most likely to be in
breach of contract and there are
thoughts that extending their
policy of not answering letters
to queries relating to non-del-
ery of goods etc. is not accept-
able. (Obviously, the policy,
where it relates to general
computing queries, is O.K. but
not where money and or goods are
involved).

The Trading Officer, Highfield
House, Denmark Road, Gloucester
GL1 3LD, has now been informed
and would no doubt be interested
if anyone else has problems.

If anyone has one of the forms
(or a copy) sent out by Format
about the conversion of subs and
the promise of a `10 voucher
could they please let me have a
copy. I was silly enough to
think Format would do the nec-
essary without problems so did
not make a copy before returning
it.I could now do with it to add
proof. Thanks, in anticipation.

On a final note, because it
seemed, just recently, two other
magazines took money but then


decided not to send any more
issues and declined to refund
outstanding subs or answer why.
In both cases the Trading Stand-
ards Office have followed up and
obtained one refund and the
other one has now informed me a
refund has been agreed. To be
fair,the one it seems the editor
had been abroad for a period, so
had simply not been here to to
answer, rather than, as I
thought, that he was avoiding
answering. The second, however,
seems to have changed their mind
after being contacted by the
Trading Office.

Please note, none of this is to
be connected in any way to
OUTLET's recent comment that the


SAM version may be discontinued,
as they have already stated
that, if they do, outstanding
subs will be sorted out, refund-
ed or whatever.

         Malcolm Perry

From: Mr. & Mrs.C. Mace,

Dear Ron,

Kevin, my 'rubella'-handicapped
son (learning difficulties is

From: D.P. Newell, READING

I have a problem with OUTPRINT
on OUTLET Extra No. 1. When 3
column printing is selected, the
printout overlaps by one char-
acter on the second column and
by two characters on the third.
Could you possibly advise me on
how to overcome this? I am using
a KODAK DICONIX 150+ printer
which emulates the EPSON FX80.

Is is possible to change the
left margin setting in OUTPRINT
(3 column printing) because I am
limited on print width in
graphics mode and lose the last
four or five characters when
printing in "Expanded" mode.
(Easier to read).


I expect these problems have
already been solved in earlier
Issues, but I only started
reading your magazine in August
1992.

Thank you in anticipation.

          D.P. Newell.

Brian Cavers to D.P. Newell

I think someone else reported a
wierd fault like this a couple
of years ago but I can't track
it down. I'm not sure if it was
ever solved. Unfortunately, as
with a lot of these contributed
programs, unless the author sees
this and can help, it is very
difficult for me to solve as it
is in machine code which could
take days and days of work even
if I had your hardware. You see,
it may be a variation in your
printer. Can anyone else help?
It may be the person(s) who had
the problem before may recollect
if it was solved. Why not use
TABLOID which really supersedes
OUTPRINT and is built into every
issue?              - Brian

From: R.R. Grimmer, WIRRAL

Dear Ron and Brian,

Many thanks for replying to my
queries as outlined in OUTLET
Issue No.63. At your suggestion
I have looked closely at the
instructions for 'JOTTER' and by
following a few dummy runs
things fell into place. I repro-
duced a printed copy of the
information and I am quite happy
with the outcome - thank you!
However, I note that the Plus D
does not feature in your print
routines!

With regard to 'TASWORD 2' - I
only possess the tape version
and wish to convert to Disc.

I have coped reasonably well
with the tape. In fact my first
successful letter was to Brian
Gaff yesterday in connection
with his advert in OUTBOARD for
his FIXIT etc. for the +2A
Spectrum,so I was quite pleased.
The only fault was that every
line was preceded by a question
mark! thus spoiling the letter.

In my endeavours to convert
'TASWORD 2' to disc I've follow-
ed the various suggestions in
OUTLETTERS from time to time
without success. So your help
with changing the SAVE syntax
enabling me to convert to disc
would be much appreciated. I am
enclosing a couple of printouts
of the Tasword 2 program where


I have tried the changes so that
you can probably see where I may
have gone wrong.

As far as utilising COL 80+ and
OUTPRINT, I have not yet been
successful. The problem as indi-
cated in OUTLET 63 still occurs.
I still get 'Invalid File Name
290:4'. I might have misguided
you in the use of the Kempson E
selection for printing. I only
made that selection in
frustration.


Sorry, I have noted the use of
the Sinclair key word token
code. Possibly you could guide
me through this procedure if you
would not mind.


I am so grateful for all your
help and I sincerely hope I am
not making a positive nuisance
of myself.

Very many thanks.

Best wishes for Christmas.

          Dick Grimmer

Brian Cavers to Dick Grimmer

In all our print routines, the
DISCIPLE option can be regarded
as synonymous with +D. If your
copy of JOTTER does not have
DISCIPLE on its printer options
then you have secured a copy off
some other version - not off the
Disciple/+D OUTLET! If so, next
time you send in a disc, remind
me that you already have a
JOTTER but it does not include
the DISCIPLE option and I will
stick one on your disc.

I can see nothing wrong with the
syntax in your Tasword listing
except the SAVE TASWORD will not
work as you are using the same
filename for BASIC and CODE!

I suggest you change the name of
the code filename to say "TAS.C"
which needs to be changed at
lines 15, 710 and 790 (insert
"TAS.C" instead of a$). Then use
the "SAVE TASWORD" option in the
Tasword menu to resave the pro-
gram. None of this would matter
until you came to use the "SAVE
TASWORD" option anyway but it is
wise to change it now!

Loading and Saving of textfiles
looks O.K.What error do you get?
I can only suggest you send the
whole thing to me on disc. Send
a note to remind me exactly what
you are doing and what the fault
is because I see loads of
correspondence and I just cannot
always remember details from
weeks before!

I've just looked back at your
letter in Issue 63 and cannot
find exactly what problem you're
getting with saving and loading
files. Since your listing looks
O.K. I'm tempted to think you're
just using the option wrongly.
When you next write, describe
EXACTLY what steps you take and
EXACTLY what are the results. If
you get an error message or if
nothing happens at all at some
stage then tell me precisely or
I cannot help you. Your listing
still has the old "just press
ENTER to load the first text on
the tape" message. This is now
obsolete as obviously this makes
no sense when loading from disc.
If you just press ENTER you will
get "invalid filename". Is that
what is happening?

On disc, you must enter a file
name if saving and the identical
name when loading.

Or is it that you save text and
the drive whirs into action and
you can load the text back and
again the drive whirs into
action but when you enter the
text editor it is empty? Please
let me know precisely.


Again, with the file loading in
COL 80+ and OUTPRINT, you say
you still get "invalid filename"
so please let me know the exact
filename you are using (or the
exact option from the menu) and
the exact disc that is in the
drive when you do so.

You ask for guidance as to how
to enter the Sinclair keyword
token "CODE" but this is given
on page 30 of my reply to you in
Issue 63. You simply press "I"
in extended mode in the input.
To spell that out, supposing you
want to enter the filename:
"editorialCODE"...

1. Select the option to enter a
   filename.

2. Type "editorial".

3. Press the EXTEND MODE key (or
   press SHIFT and SYMBOL SHIFT
   together if your keyboard has
   no EXTEND MODE key).

4. Press the "I" key to get the
   keyword "CODE". Press ENTER.

Remember, only early issues used
the keyword "CODE" for OUTLET
text files; later ones use ".#".
You need to do a CAT of the disc
to see which.

If you still get problems write
again but spell out EXACTLY what
you are doing step by step as
clearly as I have described
above so I can see where you are
going wrong.

                        - Brian

From: Mr. R.M. Hoy, BASINGSTOKE


Hello Brian and Ron,

Although I have not got a SAM
Coupe yet it seems a shame that
you are going to cease doing an
OUTLET for the SAM, just as it's
a shame SAMCo went bust again.
Why, Oh Why did they not market
this machine better in the High
Street, for example?  Then more
than likely there would be a
bigger user base and SAMCo would
still be around and you could
continue with OUTLET for it.
Also more software houses would
have supported it with serious
software etc, which is the
reason why I have not got one.


Hope is still there as I under-
stand a company called WestCoast
are making some sort of deal
with the receiver; let's hope
they learn some lesson where
others did not.

What happened to all those won-
derful collections of clip art
you once put on the OUTLET disc?
I really used to look forward to
them and without them OUTLET is
not the same for me any more.

        Yours sincerely,

            Ray Hoy

Brian Cavers to Ray Hoy

SAMCO did all they could given
their limited resources to mark-
et the SAM Coupe in the High
Street. They had almost no capi-
tal for advertising and had to
rely on public relations promos,
individual, direct contact with
dealers etc. to promote the
machine.That cannot compete with
the heavyweights who can spend
millions on tv advertising.

Our mass clip art was shelved
when the ROM INDEX was started
(still being published in the +3
OUTLET) I might start putting
more art in again when that is
finished. Meanwhile, one clip
art screen is in every issue!
                        - BRIAN.

From: Stephen Baines, SHEFFIELD

Dear OUTLET,

In Issue 63 there was a letter from G.A. Jones regarding the FD-9 disc drive. I purchased one of these from Greenweld Electro- nics and it is a wonderful drive made FOR Amstrad by one of the larger disc drive manufacturers. It is VERY quiet, and VERY reliable.
